test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 30 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the idiom that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the given sentence meaningfully.

The negotiations reached a point where both parties had to (confront the consequences of their actions) and make tough decisions.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. 'face the music'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"confront the consequences of their actions"** means to accept responsibility for something one has done and face the outcome, whether good or bad. (अपने कार्यों के परिणामों का सामना करना)

 
 
• **Example:** After being caught cheating in the exam, he had no choice but to confront the consequences of his actions.
 
 
 
• **"Face the music"** is an idiom that means to accept responsibility for one's actions or to confront the consequences of one's decisions. (परिणामों का सामना करना)
 
 
• **Example:** It's time for him to face the music for his poor financial decisions.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct idiom to replace the bracketed phrase is **'face the music'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: Break a leg** (हड्डी तोड़ दो): This is an idiom used to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance or an important event.

 
 
• **Example:** Before the play, everyone told the actors to "break a leg".
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Cut corners** (शॉर्टकट लेना): This idiom means to do something in the easiest or cheapest way, often sacrificing quality or standards.
 
 
• **Example:** The builder cut corners, and now the house has structural issues.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Get cold feet** (डर जाना): This idiom means to become nervous or hesitant about something, especially before an important event.
 
 
• **Example:** She got cold feet right before the wedding and wanted to postpone it.
 
 

118:Td68,
The correct answer is **Option 4**.
